rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks whether they recognized the ugliness of what they did to him and Benjamin: isolating and humiliating Benjamin until he could speak only in weakness.
rows.anchor: هل علمتم قبحه فتبتم عنه وفعلهم بأخيه إفراده عن يوسف وإذلاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their ignorance means failure to recognize the deed's ugliness or its consequence; their act resembled that of ignorant people, or they were then satanic children.
rows.anchor: وإنما جهلهم لأن فعلهم كان فعل الجهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph counsels them, urges repentance, and shows compassion at their helplessness rather than reproaching or blaming them.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال ذلك تنصيحا لهم وتحريضا على التوبة، وشفقة عليهم لما رأى من عجزهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says they delivered Jacob's letter seeking Benjamin's release and described Jacob's grief over losing Joseph and Benjamin, prompting Joseph's question.
rows.anchor: وقيل أعطوه كتاب يعقوب في تخليص بنيامين وذكروا له ما هو فيه من الحزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers acknowledge that God chose Joseph over them for his good appearance and complete conduct.
rows.anchor: اختارك علينا بحسن الصورة وكمال السيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They admit that their conduct toward Joseph made them sinners.
rows.anchor: إنا كنا مذنبين بما فعلنا معك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tathrib means reproach; its root is fat covering the stomach, removed like a skin, and it metaphorically describes censure that tears honor and drains dignity.
rows.anchor: لا تأنيب عليكم تفعيل من الثرب وهو الشحم الذي يغشى الكرش للإزالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Today may modify “no reproach,” emphasizing that Joseph will not blame them even when blame is expected, much less on other days.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لا أثربكم اليوم الذي هو مظنته فما ظنكم بسائر الأيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, today modifies God's forgiveness: Joseph pardoned their crime then, and they acknowledged it.
rows.anchor: لأنه صفح عن جريمتهم حينئذ واعترفوا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives minor and major sins and graciously favors the repentant.
rows.anchor: فإنه يغفر الصغائر والكبائر ويتفضل على التائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story illustrates Joseph's generosity: his brothers felt ashamed to visit after their past wrong, and he said their kinship made Egyptians honor them as Abraham's descendants.
rows.anchor: سبحان من بلغ عبدا بيع بعشرين درهما ما بلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shirt is the one Joseph was wearing; another view identifies it as an inherited shirt kept in an amulet.
rows.anchor: وقيل القميص المتوارث الذي كان في التعويذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing the shirt on Jacob's face will restore his sight.
rows.anchor: أي يرجع بصيرا أي ذا بصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph tells them to come with their father and bring every family member, including wives, children, and dependents.
rows.anchor: بنسائكم وذراريكم ومواليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those present say Jacob has long been astray through excessive love of Joseph, frequent remembrance of him, and expectation of meeting him.
rows.anchor: لفي ذهابك عن الصواب قدما بالإفراط في محبة يوسف وإكثار ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The herald is Judah; a report says he had brought Jacob the blood-stained shirt that grieved him, so he now brings this shirt to make him glad.
rows.anchor: يهوذا. روي: أنه قال كما أحزنته بحمل قميصه الملطخ بالدم إليه فأفرحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The herald may have cast the shirt on Jacob's face, or Jacob may have cast it on himself.
rows.anchor: طرح البشير القميص على وجه يعقوب عليه السلام أو يعقوب نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob recovered his sight as his strength revived.
rows.anchor: عاد بصيرا لما انتعش فيه من القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob knew from God that Joseph was alive and that joy would come.
rows.anchor: من حياة يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام، وإنزال الفرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “I know from God” begins a new statement, while the earlier statement quotes either the command not to despair of God's relief or Jacob's saying he senses Joseph's scent.
rows.anchor: وقيل إني أعلم كلام مبتدأ والمقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone who confesses a sin is entitled to be pardoned and to ask forgiveness.
rows.anchor: ومن حق المعترف بذنبه أن يصفح عنه ويسأله المفغرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob postponed seeking forgiveness until pre-dawn, night prayer, or Friday to seek an answered prayer, or until Joseph pardoned them; the wronged person's pardon is required for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: اخره إلى السحر أو إلى صلاة الليل أو إلى ليلة الجمعة تحريا لوقت الإجابة

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: A report says Jacob faced the qibla standing; an angel told him God had answered for his sons and covenanted their prophethood after him. If sound, this proves they were prophets and their wrongdoing preceded their commissioning.
rows.anchor: استقبل القبلة قائما إن الله قد أجاب دعوتك في ولدك وعقد مواثيقهم بعدك على النبوة

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: Joseph sent mounts and money for their preparations; he and Egypt's king received them with the people of Egypt, and the party entering Egypt numbered seventy-two men and women.
rows.anchor: روي أنه وجه إليه رواحل وأموالا ليتجهز إليه بمن معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The family later left Egypt with 600,570 men, excluding children and the very old.
rows.anchor: ستمائة ألف وخمسمائة وبضعة وسبعين رجلا سوى الذرية والهرمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph embraced Jacob and his aunt, treating her as his mother; she was either his father's sister or Jacob's wife after Joseph's mother, since a stepmother is called mother.
rows.anchor: ضم إليه أباه وخالته واعتنقهما نزلها منزلة الأم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording about Abraham's fathers supports treating an uncle as a father.
rows.anchor: تنزيل العم منزلة الأب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are promised safety from famine and other hardships; God's willing qualifies the safe entry, and their first arrival was at a place outside the city where Joseph met them.
rows.anchor: من القحط وأصناف المكاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prostration was a customary greeting and honor in their society.
rows.anchor: تحية وتكرمة له فإن السجود كان عندهم يجري مجراها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, they prostrated to God in gratitude on Joseph's account.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه خروا لأجله سجدا لله شكرا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parsing takes the pronoun as referring to God and the plural subject as his parents and brothers; the raising follows prostration despite being mentioned first, to emphasize their honor.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضمير لله تعالى والواو لأبويه وإخوته والرفع مؤخر عن الخرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph says the dream he saw in childhood has now been fulfilled truthfully by God.
rows.anchor: التى رأيتها أيام الصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He mentions release from prison but omits the pit to avoid blaming his brothers.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر الجب لئلا يكون تثريبا عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His family came from the desert because they kept livestock and were desert dwellers.
rows.anchor: من البادية لأنهم كانوا أصحاب المواشي وأهل البدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan sowed discord and incited them; the image comes from a rider prodding an animal to make it run.
rows.anchor: أفسد بيننا وحرش، من نزغ الرائض الدابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's subtle planning makes every difficulty yield to his will.
rows.anchor: لطيف التدبير له إذ ما من صعب إلا وتنفذ فيه مشيئته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what benefits people and acts at the proper time in the manner wisdom requires.
rows.anchor: بوجود المصالح والتدابير. { الحكيم } الذي يفعل كل شيء في وقته

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: A report says Gabriel explained that God ordered Joseph not to write Jacob because Jacob said he feared a wolf would eat Joseph; Jacob retorted that Joseph should also have feared him.
rows.anchor: فقال جبريل: الله أمرني بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph received part of Egypt's sovereignty and part of the interpretation of reports, understood as scriptures or dreams.
rows.anchor: بعض الملك وهو ملك مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Creator of the heavens and earth” is parsed either as an adjective of the addressed Lord or as a separate vocative.
rows.anchor: وانتصابه على أنه صفة المنادى أو منادى برأسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is Joseph's helper and director of his affairs, or the one who grants him blessing in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: أو الذي يتولاني بالنعمة فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawaffani means take my life; joining the righteous means either his forefathers or the righteous generally in rank and honor.
rows.anchor: اقبضني. { وألحقنى بالصلحين } من آبائي أو بعامة الصالحين في الرتبة

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: A report says Jacob lived with Joseph twenty-four years, died and was buried beside his father in Syria; Joseph returned and ruled twenty-three more years before desiring everlasting life and dying pure at age 120.
rows.anchor: أقام معه أربعا وعشرين سنة ثم توفي وأوصى أن يدفن بالشام إلى جنب أبيه

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: The Egyptians disputed Joseph's burial, placed him in a marble coffin in the Nile so its water would reach Egypt, and Moses later moved him to his ancestors' tomb.
rows.anchor: فتخاصم أهل مصر في مدفنه حتى هموا بالقتال

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: The report names Joseph's two sons by Rachel as Ephraim and Manasseh; Ephraim was Joshua's grandfather, and Rahma was Job's wife.
rows.anchor: وقد ولد له من راعيل افراثيم وميشا وهو جد يوشع بن نون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” points to the account of Joseph; the address is to the Prophet, and the phrase about unseen reports supplies the predicate of the subject.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما ذكر من نبأ يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account is revealed unseen knowledge: Muhammad was absent when Joseph's brothers plotted to put him in the well and deceive Jacob into sending him, and had not learned it from anyone; Hud 49 makes this point elsewhere.
rows.anchor: لأنك لم تحضر إخوة يوسف حين عزموا على ما هموا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people will not believe despite the Prophet's efforts and abundant signs, because they stubbornly persist in unbelief.
rows.anchor: على إيمانهم وبالغت في إظهار الآيات عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The payment they are not asked for concerns either the account being told or the Qur'an; it is no fee like storytellers receive.
rows.anchor: على الإنباء أو القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is God's admonition for all people.
rows.anchor: عظة من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Countless signs in heaven and earth demonstrate the Creator's existence, wisdom, power, and oneness, yet people observe them without reflection or taking heed.
rows.anchor: من الدلائل الدالة على وجود الصانع وحكمته وكمال قدرته وتوحيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “and the earth” is read in the nominative as a subject whose predicate is “they pass,” with its pronoun in “over it”; it is also read accusative, and one reading says “the earth, they walk upon it.”
rows.anchor: بالرفع على أنه مبتدأ خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most acknowledge God's existence and creative power but associate other worship, treat rabbis as lords, attribute adoption to God, posit light and darkness, or rely on causes.
rows.anchor: إلا وهم مشركون } بعبادة غيره أو باتخاذ الأحبار أربابا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the verse refers to the polytheists of Mecca.
rows.anchor: وقيل الآية في مشركي مكة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says it refers to hypocrites.
rows.anchor: وقيل في المنافقين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says it refers to the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: وقيل في أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sweeping punishment could cover them, or the Hour could arrive suddenly without a prior sign while they remain unaware and unprepared.
rows.anchor: عقوبة تغشاهم وتشملهم. { أو تأتيهم الساعة بغتة } فجأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's path is calling to God's oneness and preparing for the resurrection, as explained by “I call to God.”
rows.anchor: يعني الدعوة إلى التوحيد والإعداد للمعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate grammatical analysis takes the phrase as a circumstantial expression linked to the first-person pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو حال من الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling with insight means acting with clear evidence, not blindness.
rows.anchor: بيان وحجة واضحة غير عمياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I” may emphasize the hidden subject of “I call,” be the subject of the circumstantial phrase, or begin a nominal sentence whose predicate is “with insight.”
rows.anchor: لأنه حال منه أو مبتدأ خبره { على بصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “And whoever follows me” is coordinated with “I”; the Prophet declares God exalted above partners and himself free of associationism.
rows.anchor: ومن اتبعنى } عطف عليه. { وسبحان الله وما أنا من المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He declares God exalted above partners.
rows.anchor: وأنزهه تنزيها من الشركاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers were men, refuting the demand for angels as messengers; another explanation is that women were not made prophets.
rows.anchor: من قبلك إلا رجالا } رد لقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation distinguished the messengers from other people.
rows.anchor: يوحي إليهم } كما يوحي إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hafs reads “nuhi” throughout the Qur'an; Hamza and al-Kisa'i agree in Surat al-Anbiya.
rows.anchor: ووافقه حمزة والكسائي في سورة «الأنبياء»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers came from towns because town-dwellers are more knowledgeable and forbearing than Bedouins.
rows.anchor: لأن أهلها أعلم وأحلم من أهل البدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travel lets deniers see the end of earlier rejecters, or lets people absorbed in worldly life abandon their attachment to it.
rows.anchor: من المكذبين بالرسل والآيات فيحذروا تكذيبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The abode of the Hereafter” can mean its abode, its time, or its life.
rows.anchor: ولدار الحال أو الساعة أو الحياة الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who fear associationism and sins receive the better Hereafter and should use reason to recognize this.
rows.anchor: خير للذين اتقوا } الشرك والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi, Ibn Amir, Asim, and Yaqub read the address with ta, following “Say: this is my way.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وعاصم ويعقوب بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delay should not deceive people: earlier communities were given time until messengers despaired either of worldly rescue or of their people's belief as they persisted in disbelief and ease.
rows.anchor: حتى أيس الرسل عن النصر عليهم في الدنيا، أو عن إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says the messengers felt they had been given false assurance that they would be victorious.
rows.anchor: كذبتم أنفسهم حين حدثتهم بأنهم ينصرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to the people addressed: they thought the messengers had lied about the call and warning.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضمير للمرسل إليهم أي وظن المرسل إليهم أن الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further parsing assigns the first pronoun to the people and the second to the messengers, who thought they were denied promised victory and were confused.
rows.anchor: وقيل الأول للمرسل إليهم والثاني للرسل أي وظنوا أن الرسل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reportedly said the messengers thought God's promised victory had failed; if sound, Baydawi interprets this as a passing whisper in the heart.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما: أن الرسل ظنوا أنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression can be understood as an illustrative exaggeration of the long delay and respite.
rows.anchor: هذا وأن المراد به المبالغة في التراخي والإمهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Non-Kufan readers use the doubled consonant: the messengers thought the people had denied their threat.
rows.anchor: وقرأ غير الكوفيين بالتشديد أي وظن الرسل أن القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A light reading with active voice means the messengers thought what they told their people had proved false because it was delayed and left no trace.
rows.anchor: بالتخفيف وبناء الفاعل أي وظنوا أنهم قد كذبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's victory came and saved the Prophet and believers; they are left unnamed to show that only those deserving salvation are chosen, and punishment cannot be averted from criminals.
rows.anchor: من نشاء } النبي والمؤمنين وإنما لم يعينهم للدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Amir, Asim, and Yaqub read the verb as passive past; another reading is “fanjā.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم ويعقوب على لفظ الماضي المبني للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stories that teach a lesson are either those of the prophets and their peoples or Joseph and his brothers; they benefit people of sound reason, free of habit and sensory attachment.
rows.anchor: لقد كان فى قصصهم } في قصص الأنبياء وأممهم أو في قصة يوسف وإخوته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is no fabricated account but confirms earlier divine books.
rows.anchor: ما كان القرآن حديثا يفترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It explains every religious matter people need, directly or indirectly, and gives believers guidance from error and mercy for both worlds.
rows.anchor: ما من أمر ديني إلا وله سند من القرآن بوسط أو بغير وسط

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet recommends teaching Surat Yusuf to servants, family, and those under one's authority; God will ease a Muslim's death pangs and give strength not to envy another Muslim.
rows.anchor: علموا أرقاءكم سورة يوسف، فإنه أيما مسلم تلاها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report says the sura has 111 verses, excepting the passage beginning “They were about to tempt you” through eight verses.
rows.anchor: وقيل إلا قوله تعالى: { وإن كادوا ليفتنونك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subhan names glorification and transcendence; as a proper name it is severed from annexation and is indeclinable. A cited line illustrates the word subhan.
rows.anchor: سبحان اسم بمعنى التسبيح { الذى } هو التنزيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subhan is accusative under an unexpressed verb; placing it first declares God incapable of none of what follows.
rows.anchor: وانتصابه بفعل متروك إظهاره، وتصدير الكلام به للتنزيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asra and sara mean the same; laylan is an adverb of time, and its indefinite form indicates the journey took only a short part of the night, as does the reading “min al-layl.”
rows.anchor: أسرى } وسرى بمعنى، و { ليلا } نصب على الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report has the Prophet in the Hijr by the Kaaba between sleep and wakefulness when Gabriel brought the Buraq, supporting a departure from the Sacred Mosque itself.
rows.anchor: بينا أنا في المسجد الحرام في الحجر عند البيت بين النائم واليقظان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “the Sacred Mosque” means the whole sanctuary, which is a mosque, surrounds the mosque, or is named to parallel the destination; another report places the Prophet at Umm Hani's house after night prayer, returning the same night after meeting the prophets.
rows.anchor: أو «من الحرم» وسماه المسجد الحرام لأنه كله مسجد

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: The report says Quraysh marveled and some believers apostatized; Abu Bakr affirmed the Prophet and was called al-Siddiq, after which the Prophet described Jerusalem and a caravan's camels and arrival, but the disbelievers called it clear magic. This was a year before Hijra.
rows.anchor: فقال: إن كان قال لقد صدق، فقالوا: أتصدقه على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People disagreed whether the journey was a dream or occurred awake, and whether it was by spirit or body; most held that his body traveled to Jerusalem and ascended to the heavens and the Lote Tree.
rows.anchor: واختلف في أنه كان في المنام أو في اليقظة بروحه أو بجسده، والأكثر على أنه أسرى بجسده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the objection that bodily travel was impossible, Baydawi argues that the Sun's diameter is over 160 times Earth's and its edge travels across that distance in under a second; bodies accept accidents equally, so God can create such speed in the Prophet or his mount. Amazement is inherent in miracles.
rows.anchor: أن الله قادر على كل الممكنات فيقدر أن يخلق مثل هذه الحركة السريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Farthest Mosque is Jerusalem, since at that time there was no mosque beyond it.
rows.anchor: بيت المقدس لأنه لم يكن حينئذ وراءه مسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its surroundings are blessed in religion and worldly life as a site of revelation and prophetic worship, and as a region of rivers and trees.
rows.anchor: ببركات الدين والدنيا لأنه مهبط الوحي ومتعبد الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs included traveling a month's distance in part of a night, seeing Jerusalem, the prophets appearing, and seeing their stations; the shift to first-person plural magnifies the blessings and signs.
rows.anchor: كذهابه في برهة من الليل مسيرة شهر ومشاهدته بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has “li-yuriyahu” with third-person yā.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «ليريه» بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears Muhammad's words and sees his actions, honoring and drawing him near accordingly.
rows.anchor: لأقوال محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم. { البصير } بأفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That you not take” can be parsed as a complement introduced by an, as in a written instruction; Abu Amr reads the verb in the third person.
rows.anchor: على أن لا تتخذوا كقولك: كتبت إليك

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads “that they not take” with yā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بالياء على «أن لا يتخذوا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wakil is a lord to whom one entrusts one's affairs.
rows.anchor: ربا تكلون إليه أموركم غيري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhurriyyata can be an accusative of specification or a vocative if the prohibition is read with second-person ta; it may also be an object of “take,” with “apart from me” modifying “protector.”
rows.anchor: نصب على الاختصاص أو النداء أن قرىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead be nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject or as a substitute for the subject pronoun; another reading has kasra on the dhāl.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالرفع على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase recalls God's favor in saving Noah's descendants from drowning by carrying their ancestors in the Ark.
rows.anchor: وفيه تذكير بأنعام الله تعالى عليهم في إنجاء آبائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He” refers to Noah: he praised God in all circumstances; his salvation with his companions hints that gratitude brought it and urges descendants to imitate him.
rows.anchor: إن نوحا عليه السلام. { كان عبدا شكورا } يحمد الله تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to Moses.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضمير لموسى عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God communicated to the Children of Israel an irrevocable decree in the Torah.
rows.anchor: وأوحينا إليهم وحيا مقضيا مبتوتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic prediction can answer an unspoken oath, or the irrevocable decree can be treated as an oath.
rows.anchor: جواب قسم محذوف، أو قضينا على إجراء القضاء المبتوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first corruption was violating Torah rulings and killing Isaiah, or Jeremiah; the second was killing Zechariah and John and attempting Jesus' death.
rows.anchor: إفسادتين أولاهما مخالفة أحكام التوراة وقتل شعياء وقيل أرمياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their arrogance means either refusing God's obedience or oppressing people.
rows.anchor: ولتستكبرن عن طاعة الله تعالى أو لتظلمن الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first promise is the promised punishment for their first corruption.
rows.anchor: وعد عقاب أولاهما. { بعثنا عليكم عبادا لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attackers are identified as Nebuchadnezzar, an agent of Loharasp in Babylon, with his forces.
rows.anchor: بختنصر عامل لهراسف على بابل وجنوده

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies the attackers as Jalut al-Jazari.
rows.anchor: وقيل جالوت الجزري

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as Sennacherib of Nineveh.
rows.anchor: وقيل سنحاريب من أهل نينوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “People of severe might” means powerful and fierce in war; “they ranged” means they moved about searching for Israelites, with a variant reading using ḥāʾ.
rows.anchor: ذوي قوة وبطش في الحرب شديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant uses ḥāʾ; the two forms are related.
rows.anchor: فترددوا لطلبكم. وقرىء بالحاء المهملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They searched homes to kill and raid, killed leaders, captured children, burned the Torah, and destroyed the temple.
rows.anchor: وسطها للقتل والغارة فقتلوا كبارهم وسبوا صغارهم وحرقوا التوراة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Because Mu'tazilites deny that God empowers unbelievers to commit such acts, they interpret the sending as allowing it by not preventing them.
rows.anchor: والمعتزلة لما منعوا تسليط الله الكافر على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment promise was bound to be carried out.
rows.anchor: وكان وعد عقابهم لا بد أن يفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “return” means restored power and victory over those sent against them.
rows.anchor: أي الدولة والغلبة. { عليهم } على الذين بعثوا عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Bahman son of Asfandiyar inherited from his grandfather Gushtasb son of Loharasp, pitied the Israelites, returned captives to Syria, and installed Daniel, who overcame Nebuchadnezzar's followers; another says God gave David victory over Jalut.
rows.anchor: بأن ألقى الله في قلوب بهمن بن اسفنديار لما ورث الملك من جده كشتاسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Nafir” means those who go out with a man from his people, or a group assembled to go to battle.
rows.anchor: والنفير من ينفر مع الرجل من قومه وقيل جمع نفروهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good conduct benefits the doer through its reward, while bad conduct harms the doer through its consequence; the feminine pronoun pairs the wording.
rows.anchor: لأن ثوابه لها. { وإن أسأتم فلها } فإن وباله عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later promise is punishment for the second corruption.
rows.anchor: وعد عقوبة المرة الآخرة. { فولوا وجوهكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enemy's mission is to make distress visible on their faces; the subject is omitted because its earlier mention implies it.
rows.anchor: أي يجعلوها بادية آثار المساءة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Abu Bakr read the verb in the singular; its subject may be the promise, sending, or God, supported by al-Kisa'i's first-person plural reading; other variants alter the verb form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة وأبو بكر «ليسوء» على التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about entering the mosque is linked to an omitted “We sent them”; “to destroy” means to ruin what they conquered or their period of rule.
rows.anchor: متعلق بمحذوف هو بعثناهم. { كما دخلوه أول مرة وليتبروا } ليهلكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Persians returned under the Babylonian king Jūdarz or Ḥardūs; finding blood bubbling at the altar, they killed thousands until it was identified as John's blood, and it stopped when the king asked John to quiet it by God's leave.
rows.anchor: فسألهم عنه فقالوا: دم قربان لم يقبل منا فقال: ما صدقوني فقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may show mercy after the second punishment; if they relapse, he will punish them a third time.
rows.anchor: بعد المرة الآخرة. { وإن عدتم } نوبة أخرى. { عدنا } مرة ثالثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their later relapse was rejecting Muhammad and seeking to kill him; God answered by killing Qurayza, expelling Nadir, and imposing tribute on the rest in this world.
rows.anchor: وقد عادوا بتكذيب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وقصد قتله فعاد الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hasir means a prison from which they can never escape, or a carpet-like mat.
rows.anchor: أبد الآباد. وقيل بساطا كما يبسط الحصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an guides to the most upright state or way among states or ways.
rows.anchor: للحالة أو الطريقة التي هي أقوم الحالات أو الطرق

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read yubashshiru in the lightened form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي { ويبشر } بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about unbelievers may coordinate with the promise of great reward, giving believers two tidings: their reward and their enemies' punishment; or it coordinates with “gives glad tidings,” with “informs” understood.
rows.anchor: عطف على { أن لهم أجرا كبيرا } ، والمعنى أنه يبشر المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When angry, a person may call for evil against self, family, or property, or ask for what seems good but proves evil; such calls resemble calls for good.
rows.anchor: ويدعو الله تعالى عند غضبه بالشر على نفسه وأهله وماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People rush toward each thought that occurs to them without considering its consequence.
rows.anchor: يسارع إلى كل ما يخطر بباله لا ينظر عاقبته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies the human as Adam, who tried to stand before the spirit had reached beyond his navel and fell.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد آدم عليه الصلاة والسلام فإنه لما انتهى الروح إلى سرته

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet gave a captive to Sawda bint Zam'a; pitying his groans, she loosened his bonds and he escaped. The Prophet prayed that a curse he regretted be made mercy, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: دفع أسيرا إلى سودة بنت زمعة فرحمته لأنينه فأرخت كتافه، فهرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the human is an unbeliever who mockingly hastens punishment, like al-Nadr ibn al-Harith's prayer; it was answered and he was executed as a captive at Badr.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد بالإنسان الكافر وبالدعاء استعجاله بالعذاب استهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordered alternation of night and day demonstrates the powerful, wise Creator.
rows.anchor: تدلان على القادر الحكيم بتعاقبهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first explanation takes night itself as the sign erased by illumination, with the possessive construction serving to explain the relation.
rows.anchor: أي الآية التي هي الليل، بالإشراق والإضافة فيهما للتبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daylight made “seeing” can mean bright, enabling people to see, or seeing its people, like saying a man's household is brave when he is brave.
rows.anchor: مضيئة أو مبصرة للناس من أبصره فبصر، أو مبصرا أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the two signs are moon and sun: the moon's light is effaced by darkness or gradually diminished to new moon, while the sun shines to reveal things.
rows.anchor: وقيل الآيتان القمر والشمس، وتقدير الكلام وجعلنا نيري الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daylight lets people seek their livelihood and see their work clearly.
rows.anchor: لتطلبوا في بياض النهار أسباب معاشكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternation or movements of night and day let people count years and calculate time.
rows.anchor: باختلافهما أو بحركاتهما. { عدد السنين والحساب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has explained clearly everything needed for religious and worldly affairs.
rows.anchor: تفتقرون إليه في أمر الدين والدنيا. { فصلناه تفصيلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's bird is his deeds and decreed lot; bird omens become a metaphor for whatever causes good or evil, including God's decree and human action.
rows.anchor: عمله وما قدر له كأنه طير إليه من عش الغيب ووكر القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its being bound to the neck indicates the lot's unavoidable attachment.
rows.anchor: فى عنقه } لزوم الطوق في عنقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book on Judgment Day is either the record of one's deeds or the self imprinted by actions, since chosen acts shape the soul and repetition forms dispositions.
rows.anchor: هي صحيفة عمله أو نفسه المنتقشة بآثار أعماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book's grammatical status can be an object or circumstantial expression from an omitted object pronoun referring to the bird; Yaqub's reading supports this, and other readings vary between forms of “bring out.”
rows.anchor: ونصبه بأنه مفعول أو حال من مفعول محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Spread open” means the covering is removed; the terms may both describe the book, or the second may be circumstantial, and Ibn Amir reads “yalqāhu” in a passive construction.
rows.anchor: لكشف الغطاء، وهما صفتان للكتاب، أو { يلقه } صفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Read your book” assumes an omitted verb of saying.
rows.anchor: اقرأ كتبك } على إرادة القول. { كفى بنفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person suffices as his own judge today: the bā in “by yourself” is extra, and “accountant” is a specification; the word means reckoner or one who suffices, hence witness.
rows.anchor: أي كفى نفسك، والباء مزيدة و { حسيبا } تمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine form reflects the usual male roles of accounting and testimony, or treats the soul as a person.
rows.anchor: وتذكيره على أن الحساب والشهادة مما يتولاه الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance benefits only the person who follows it, and error harms only the person who strays.
rows.anchor: لا ينجي اهتداؤه غيره ولا يردي ضلاله سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No burden-bearing soul carries another's burden; each bears only its own.
rows.anchor: ولا تحمل نفس حاملة وزرا وزر نفس أخرى، بل إنما تحمل وزرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not punish before sending a messenger to establish proofs and laws, demonstrating that there is no obligation before revealed law.
rows.anchor: يبين الحجج ويمهد الشرائع فيلزمهم الحجة، وفيه دليل على أن لا وجوب قبل الشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means either God wills to destroy people to execute a prior decree, or that the appointed time is near, as a sick person's illness intensifies near death.
rows.anchor: وإذا تعلقت إرادتنا بإهلاك قوم لإنفاذ قضائنا السابق، أو دنا وقته المقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to the affluent was to obey through a messenger, as context shows and because corruption is disobedience, the opposite of obedience.
rows.anchor: متنعميها بالطاعة على لسان رسول بعثناه إليهم، ويدل على ذلك ما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative that God ordered them to sin relies on an idiom where an order is followed by its execution; here it means causing or inducing sin, such as by blessings that made them insolent.
rows.anchor: وقيل أمرناهم بالفسق لقوله: { ففسقوا فيها } كقولك أمرته فقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the verb as “made numerous,” supported by a saying about prolific production; Yaqub's reading and a report from Abu Amr support this form.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه كثرنا يقال: أمرت الشيء وآمرته فأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead derive from making them rulers; the affluent are singled out because others follow them and because they are quicker to folly and more capable of wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون منقولا من أمر بالضم أمارة أي جعلناهم أمراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The decree of punishment takes effect on arrival, when their sins become manifest, or when they are immersed in sins.
rows.anchor: كلمة العذاب السابقة بحلوله، أو بظهور معاصيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroys the town by destroying its people and laying waste to its homes.
rows.anchor: أهلكناها بإهلاك أهلها وتخريب ديارهم
